text: At its meeting held on November 14, 2017, North York Community Council adopted without amendment Item NY26.22 and, in so doing, denied the installation of speed humps on King High Avenue and Allingham Gardens. As the staff recommendations do not reflect the requirements of the residents on these streets, it is recommended that the Item be re-opened and amended to address these concerns.

North Community Council: 1. Deleted Parts 1 and 2 of the decision on Item NY26.22 and adopted instead the following: "1. The Acting Director of Transportation Services, North York District request the City Clerk to poll eligible householders on King High Avenue, between Invermay Avenue and Allingham Gardens, and on Allingham Gardens, between King High Avenue and Wilson Avenue, to determine whether residents support the installation of traffic calming, in accordance with the City of Toronto Traffic Calming Policy. 2. Subject to favourable results of the poll, the City Solicitor: a. prepare a by-law to alter sections of the roadway on King High Avenue, between Invermay Avenue and Allingham Gardens, and on Allingham Gardens, between King High Avenue and Wilson Avenue, for traffic calming purposes, generally as shown in the speed hump plan that Transportation Services circulates to…
